_: The narration, cut into lines. One line is one caption and one TTS clip,
which is what keeps the two in sync: the caption cannot drift from the
audio because they are built from the same array.
`scene` names the footage the line plays over. `hold` is extra seconds of
footage after the line finishes, for shots that need to breathe.
Read at about 145 words a minute. Timings are derived from the rendered
audio, never guessed, so a rewrite reflows the whole video automatically.

lines.text: Every day, crypto has a worst performer.
In sFace, that coin becomes the level. This ground is its real twenty four hour chart.
Nobody drew this. The market did, at midnight, and it will draw a different one tomorrow.
This cycle has been a long run of things going quiet.
Projects winding down, tokens going to nothing, and another thread every week explaining why it was always going to happen.
sFace is what you would rather look at. A rescue game where the wreck is the market, and the people trapped in it are the accounts who were arguing about it hours ago.
It plays as a twin stick shooter. Fly the day's chart, pull people out, reach extraction before the clock.
Fear and Greed decides how crowded the sky is, so a fearful market is a genuinely harder level.
Halfway through, the chart leaves. The same price data, drawn as bars, is already a skyline, so the gaps between the bars become streets.
There is a car. It is twice as fast and heard from twice as far.
Then the game stops asking you to shoot, and starts asking you to read.
Four posts that genuinely went out today. One of them explains the day. Pick it and the panel flips. Pick wrong and the whole street starts walking toward you.
Every post links back to the original. Nothing here is written by us and put in somebody's mouth.
The finale is a third kind of world. Concentric walls around a core, worked inward.
No weapon opens a gate. Each wall asks about the projects that were here before this cycle and will be here after it.
Reach one and it tells you how it is holding up. Fly past it and you can still reach the wall. You simply cannot answer it.
It is built for Nimiq Pay. Your wallet is your name, so a score belongs to an address instead of a device anyone can throw away.
Every run is signed, and every row on the board publishes its signature, so anyone can check it without trusting us.
Pull your closest mutuals into a clan and pool your Face. Stake a friend on the exact same seed and settle it in NIM, wallet to wallet. sFace never holds funds.
Clear all seven stages and the camera pulls back, until the day you just fought through is a notch on a long climb.
Two trillion is still early. That is the only thing this game argues, and it waits until you have earned it.
sFace. The market builds the level. Play it at sface dot site, and the code is on GitHub.
